THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST NOW THAT BLOOM HAS ARRIVED: THERE IS NO 'Bloom' KEY IN THE BUILDER AND THERE MUST NEVER BE ONE. The surname is five people -- Leopold, Marion, Milly, Rudolph and Rudy -- AND A MOUNTAIN RANGE: 4:38 is SLIEVE BLOOM, in Offaly, in the middle of Bloom's own thoughts. Every mention is keyed on a longer phrase (Mr Leopold Bloom, Mr Bloom, Mrs Marion Bloom, Milly Bloom, Mr and Mrs L. M. Bloom) and a test asserts the bare surname never becomes a key. Molly, Marion, Poldy, Milly, Boylan, Dignam and Tweedy are all keyed for the same reason; the comments in build_ulysses.py name the other bearer in each case.

THE FINDING THE RELEASE OWNER MOST NEEDS, unchanged: THE MODERN EDITION OF ULYSSES IS A REWRITE AND IT CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Episode 1: it deletes Chrysostomos (1:9), Mercury's hat (1:293) and Chuck Loyola (1:101), and substitutes Swinburne for Algy and William for Billy. Episode 3: it NAMES FOUR PEOPLE JOYCE DID NOT NAME -- Aristotle (3:0), Brian Boru (3:57, for 'the Dalcassians'), Deasy (3:10) and Queen Victoria (3:94) -- so BRIAN BORU EXISTS IN THE MODERN EDITION ALONE and is an omittedEntity for the ORIGINAL. Episode 4: it DELETES TWO DUBLIN NAMES at 4:37, where 'they blossom out as Adam Findlaters or Dan Tallons' becomes 'successful businessmen', so ADAM FINDLATER is an omittedEntity for the MODERN edition; it also drops 'Hanlon's' at 4:13. Check both editions before writing any card that turns on a name.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY, NOT JUST THIS ONE: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. It has now bitten twice here: '_Los Demiurgos_' at 3:1 (invisible in both editions) and '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' at 4:162 (bound in the modern edition, silently not in the older one -- found by the edition-asymmetry census). Both are keyed now, and test_no_alias_in_this_package_is_hidden_by_italics compares every alias under both guards over the read episodes. Run over all 18 episodes it reports two more, both still ahead: STEPHEN at 15:1133, inside a stage direction, which will need a key when Circe is read, and PATRICE at 16:212, which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice called Ireland for short', and will need suppressing.

THE OCCURRENCE LIST KEEPS PAYING. In episode 4 it found that the HEAD CENTRE of episode 3 -- whom that episode names only by his office -- IS NAMED AT 4:159: 'the chap in the paybox there got away James Stephens, they say'. The card was rewritten and the entity now binds at 4:159, 8:133, 12:234 and 15:433; 9:126 is a DIFFERENT James Stephens, the writer doing some clever sketches, and gets no card. It also joined BANNON up across three episodes: he sends a card from Westmeath in episode 1 about a photo girl, and Milly writes home from Mullingar in episode 4 about a young student named Bannon. Same man.

Deliberate gaps in episode 4, each pinned by a test: THE CAT has more dialogue than most of the cast and is not cast; Saint Joseph's National school at 4:38 is not Joseph the Joiner; 'O'Brien.' at 4:159 and 'Did Roberts pay you yet?' at 4:164 are bare surnames the text never settles; and the shops of Dublin keep their owners' names and are not people (Buckley's, Denny's, Boland's, Plasto's, Drago's, M'Auley's, Andrews, Cassidy's, Thornton's). Larry O'Rourke and Dlugacz ARE cast, because both are men in the scene. No edition byte was touched; five source defects are recorded and not repaired. This lane never sets appStatus.
